entries.title: Psalms 119:1
segments:
PSALM CXIX. 
 
  Because this psalm was very large, and the matter of it of the greatest   importance, the psalmist thought fit to divide it into two and twenty   several parts, according to the number of the Hebrew letters, that   he might both prevent tediousness, and fix it in the memory.  Each part   consists of eight verses.  All the verses of the first part beginning   with Aleph, all the verses of the second with Beth, and so on.   It is observable, that the word of God is here called by the names of   law, statutes, precepts or commandments, judgments, ordinances,   righteousness, testimonies, way and word.  By which variety, he   designed to express the nature and perfection of God's word.  It is   called his word, as revealed by him to us; his way, as   prescribed by him for us to walk in; his law, as binding us to   obedience; his statutes, as declaring his authority of giving us   laws; his precepts as directing our duty; his ordinances, as   ordained by him; his righteousness, as exactly agreeable to God's   righteous nature and will; his judgments, as proceeding from the   great judge of the world, and being his judicial sentence to which all   men must submit; and his testimonies, as it contains the witness of   God's will, and of man's duty.  And there is but one of these one   hundred and seventy six verses, in which one or other of these titles   is not found.  The general scope and design of this psalm is, to   magnify the law and make it honourable: to shew the excellency and   usefulness of divine revelation, and recommend it to us, by the   psalmist's own example, who speaks by experience of the benefits of it,   for which he praises God, and earnestly prays for the continuance of   God's grace, to direct and quicken him in his way.

entries.title: Psalms 119:6
segments: V. 6. Respect-A due respect, which implies hearty affection, diligent study, and constant practice.  To all-So as not to allow myself in any known sin, or in the neglect of any known duty.

entries.title: Psalms 119:7
segments: V. 7. When-When by thy good spirit I shall he more fitly instructed in the meaning of thy word.

entries.title: Psalms 119:8
segments: V. 8. Forsake me not-For then I shall fall into the foulest sins.

entries.title: Psalms 119:9
segments: V. 9. A young man-Or, any man.  But he names the young man, because such are commonly void of wisdom and experience, and exposed to many and great temptations.  Cleanse-Purge himself from all filthiness of flesh and spirit.

entries.title: Psalms 119:11
segments: V. 11. Hid-I have laid it up in my mind like a choice treasure, to be ready upon all occasions to counsel, quicken or caution me.

entries.title: Psalms 119:17
segments: V. 17. Live-Safely and comfortably.

entries.title: Psalms 119:18
segments: V. 18. Open-Enlighten my mind by the light of thy Holy Spirit, and dispel all ignorance and error.  Behold-Those great and marvellous depths of Divine wisdom and goodness, and those profound mysteries of Christ, and God's grace to mankind, and of that everlasting state, which are not to be known but by Divine illumination.

entries.title: Psalms 119:19
segments: V. 19. A stranger-I am not here as in my home, but as a pilgrim travelling homeward in a strange land.  Commandments-Which are my chief support and guide in my pilgrimage.

entries.title: Psalms 119:20
segments: V. 20. Breaketh-Faints, as it frequently does, when a thing vehemently desired is delayed.  Judgments-To a more sound knowledge and serious practice of them.

entries.title: Psalms 119:21
segments: V. 21. The proud-Obstinate and presumptuous sinners, who sin with an high hand.  Err-Or, wander, knowingly or wilfully.

entries.title: Psalms 119:25
segments: V. 25. The dust-I am in danger of present death: I am like one laid in the grave.  Quicken-Preserve my life, or raise me out of the dust. Word-According to thy promise.

entries.title: Psalms 119:26
segments: V. 26. My ways-My sins; and all my cares, and fears, and troubles.

entries.title: Psalms 119:27
segments: V. 27. Understand-More throughly.

entries.title: Psalms 119:28
segments: V. 28. Melteth-Like wax before the fire.

entries.title: Psalms 119:29
segments: V. 29. Grant me-Vouchsafe me an accurate knowledge of thy word, and let me govern myself by it in all things.

entries.title: Psalms 119:30
segments: V. 30. Laid-Or, set before me as a mark to aim at; as a rule to direct me.

entries.title: Psalms 119:32
segments: V. 32. Run-I will obey thy precepts with all readiness, fervency, and diligence.  Enlarge-When thou shalt replenish my heart with wisdom, and love to thee and thy law.

entries.title: Psalms 119:36
segments: V. 36. Covetousness-He mentions this in particular, because it is most opposite to God's testimonies, and does most commonly hinder men from receiving his word, and from profiting by it: and because it is most pernicious, as being the root of all evil.

entries.title: Psalms 119:37
segments: V. 37. Vanity-The vain things of this present world, such as riches, honours, pleasures: from beholding them, with desire or affection. Quicken-Make me lively, vigorous and fervent in thy service.

entries.title: Psalms 119:38
segments: V. 38. Stablish-Confirm and perform thy promises.

entries.title: Psalms 119:39
segments: V. 39. I fear-For my instability in thy ways; which in respect to my own weakness, I have great cause to fear.

entries.title: Psalms 119:40
segments: V. 40. Longed-After a more solid knowledge and constant performance of them.  In-According to thy faithfulness.

entries.title: Psalms 119:43
segments: V. 43. Take not-Do not deal so with me, that I shall be ashamed to mention thy word.  Judgments-In thy word.

entries.title: Psalms 119:45
segments: V. 45. At liberty-Enjoy great freedom and comfort in thy ways.

entries.title: Psalms 119:48
segments: V. 48. Lift up-To receive and embrace thy precepts and promises.

entries.title: Psalms 119:49
segments: V. 49. Thy word-Thy promises.

entries.title: Psalms 119:52
segments: V. 52. Judgments-Thy ancient dispensations to the children of men in punishing the ungodly.

entries.title: Psalms 119:53
segments: V. 53. Horror-A mixed passion, made up of abhorrence of their sins, and dread and sorrow at the consideration of the judgments of God coming upon them.

entries.title: Psalms 119:54
segments: V. 54. The house-In this world, wherein I am a stranger and pilgrim, as all my fathers were.

entries.title: Psalms 119:55
segments: V. 55. Thy name-Thy holy nature and attributes, thy blessed word, and thy wonderful works.  In the night-When darkness causes fear in others, I took pleasure in remembering thee; and when others gave themselves up to sleep, my thoughts and affections were working towards thee.

entries.title: Psalms 119:56
segments: V. 56. This-This comfortable remembrance.

entries.title: Psalms 119:57
segments: V. 57. Said-I have professed and owned it.

entries.title: Psalms 119:59
segments: V. 59. Thought-I seriously considered both my former courses, and my duty in all my future actions.

entries.title: Psalms 119:61
segments: V. 61. Robbed-Done me many injuries, for my respect to thy law.

entries.title: Psalms 119:66
segments: V. 66. Judgment-Whereby I may rightly discern between truth and falsehood.  Knowledge-A spiritual experimental knowledge.

entries.title: Psalms 119:70
segments: V. 70. Fat-They are stupid and insensible.

entries.title: Psalms 119:74
segments: V. 74. Glad-For the encouragement they have by my example to trust in God.  See me-Alive and in safety.  Word-In thy promise, and have not been disappointed of my hope.

entries.title: Psalms 119:75
segments: V. 75. Judgments-Thy corrections.  Of faithfulness-In pursuance of thy promises, and in order to my good.

entries.title: Psalms 119:79
segments: V. 79. Known-Loved and practised them.

entries.title: Psalms 119:80
segments: V. 80. Sound-That I may love and obey them sincerely, constantly, and universally.

entries.title: Psalms 119:81
segments: V. 81. Fainteth-With long desire and earnest expectation.

entries.title: Psalms 119:83
segments: V. 83. Bottle-A leathern bottle.  My natural moisture is dryed and burnt up.

entries.title: Psalms 119:84
segments: V. 84. The days-The days of my life.  I have but a little while to live; give me some respite before I die.

entries.title: Psalms 119:85
segments: V. 85. Who-Who have no respect to thy law.

entries.title: Psalms 119:86
segments: V. 86. Faithful-Just and true.

entries.title: Psalms 119:89
segments: V. 89. In heaven-With thee in thy heavenly habitation.

entries.title: Psalms 119:91
segments: V. 91. They-The heaven and the earth.  Ordinances-As thou hast appointed.  For-All things are subject to thy power and pleasure.

entries.title: Psalms 119:96
segments: V. 96. Perfection-Of the greatest and most perfect enjoyments in this world.  Commandment-Thy word; one part of it being put for the whole. Broad-Or, large, both for extent, and for continuance: it is useful to all persons: it is of everlasting truth and efficacy; it will never deceive those who trust to it, as all worldly things will, but will make men happy both here and for ever.

entries.title: Psalms 119:100
segments: V. 100. Because-The practice of religion is the best way to understand it.

entries.title: Psalms 119:102
segments: V. 102. Taught me-By thy blessed spirit, illuminating my mind, and working upon my heart.

entries.title: Psalms 119:108
segments: V. 108. Offerings-The sacrifices of prayer and praise.

entries.title: Psalms 119:109
segments: V. 109. Is-Exposed to perpetual danger.

entries.title: Psalms 119:118
segments: V. 118. Deceit-Their deceitful devices, shall bring that destruction upon themselves which they design for others.

entries.title: Psalms 119:121
segments: V. 121. Judgment, &c.-Just judgment.

entries.title: Psalms 119:122
segments: V. 122. Surety-Do thou undertake and plead my cause.

entries.title: Psalms 119:123
segments: V. 123. The word-For the performance of thy faithful or merciful promise.

entries.title: Psalms 119:126
segments: V. 126. To work-To put forth thy power for the restraint of evil-doers. They-The wicked.  Made void-Or, abrogated thy law, have openly cast off its authority.

entries.title: Psalms 119:127
segments: V. 127. Therefore-Because the general apostacy of others makes this duty more necessary.

entries.title: Psalms 119:129
segments: V. 129. Wonderful-In regard of the deep mysteries, the most excellent directions, and the exceeding great and precious promises of God contained in them.

entries.title: Psalms 119:131
segments: V. 131. Panted-I thirst after thy precepts, and pursue them eagerly.

entries.title: Psalms 119:133
segments: V. 133. Steps-My motions and actions.

entries.title: Psalms 119:136
segments: V. 136. Rivers-Plentiful tears, witness of my deep sorrow for God's dishonour, and for the miseries which sinners bring upon themselves.

entries.title: Psalms 119:140
segments: V. 140. Pure-Without the least mixture of falsehood.

entries.title: Psalms 119:142
segments: V. 142. Everlasting-The same in all ages and places.

entries.title: Psalms 119:143
segments: V. 143. Trouble-Outward troubles and anguish of spirit.

entries.title: Psalms 119:148
segments: V. 148. Watches-The middle watch, which was set in the middle of the night; and the morning watch, which was set some hours before the dawning of the day.

entries.title: Psalms 119:149
segments: V. 149. Judgment-According to thy word.

entries.title: Psalms 119:150
segments: V. 150. Nigh-To me, they are at hand and ready to seize upon me. Are far-They cast away from them all thoughts of thy law.

entries.title: Psalms 119:152
segments: V. 152. Of old-By long experience.  Founded-Thou hast established them upon everlasting foundations.

entries.title: Psalms 119:160
segments: V. 160. The beginning-From the beginning of the world.

entries.title: Psalms 119:161
segments: V. 161. But-But I feared thine offence and displeasure more than their wrath.

entries.title: Psalms 119:164
segments: V. 164. Seven times-Many times; a certain number being put for an uncertain.

entries.title: Psalms 119:165
segments: V. 165. Offend-Heb. they shall have no stumbling-block, at which they shall stumble and fall into mischief.

entries.title: Psalms 119:175
segments: V. 175. Judgments-Thy word or testimonies, which are the only ground of my hope in thy help.
